learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected under 0.1 distance after five steps at learning rate 1.1 and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Set rate 1.1 and ran five steps: distance 2.488, factor 1.2. Set 0.5, which reset steps, and took one step: distance zero, factor zero. Set 1.0 and ran five steps: distance remained one, factor one. Reveal retained original divergent trajectory.
observations.reveal: Corrected about 2.5. Lists alternating divergent iterates and distance multiplier absolute value of 1 minus twice the rate. Connects tested exact-bottom and neutral-oscillation rates to convergence threshold. Also describes untested 0.4 rate.
observations.visual: Inspected inline divergent-path screenshot: purple dashed zigzags cross the bowl and grow away from its bottom, with distance 2.488 and factor 1.2. Controls and labels legible. Trust count 3/3 ignored.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: Precise numerical question but gradient update notation assumes substantial prior algebra.
prediction.evidence: Rate 1.1 update equation before the prediction.

interaction.reason: Divergent, exact-solution and neutral-boundary rates visibly distinguish three mechanisms.
interaction.evidence: 1.1 grows, 0.5 reaches zero, 1.0 stays at one.

payoff.reason: Connects actual trajectories to multiplier and convergence boundary.
payoff.evidence: Alternating sequence, zero/one/1.2 factors and steepness limit.

clarity.reason: Named rates, step count and explicit factor make tested path understandable.
clarity.evidence: Reset on rate change and screenshot readouts.

transfer.reason: Reusable step-size caution supplied without a concrete new loss function or applicability calculation.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Small-distance prediction reversed by oversized steps diverging.

visualExplanation.reason: Bowl and zigzag path carry overshooting and growing-distance mechanism.
visualExplanation.evidence: Divergence screenshot plus three rate contrasts.

playfulness.reason: Rate choices and single/batch stepping allow reversible experiments.
playfulness.evidence: Three rates and both step controls tested.

practicalValue.evidence: Oversized gradient steps fail to converge.

depth.reason: Divergence, exact landing and neutral oscillation are distinct observed cases.

complexity.reason: Coordinates derivative-based update, signed iterates, distance factor and stability threshold.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Several dependent algebra and optimization relations.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Low: rate presets and step controls.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: high: eta, square loss, assignment arrow and absolute value

whyCool: A rate of 0.5 lands exactly at the bottom, while doubling it to one makes the point bounce forever at the same distance.
caveat: Only the scalar square loss is tested; other curvature and loss functions remain unknown.
